messages.author: e32484f448e128cc
messages.subject: child variable filename?
parts:
Hi there,
Sorry --- this may be a trivial question. But I'm trying to compile a .Rnw file which is made by a main document and should include several other .Rnw files. But the files to be included should be randomly selected from a list of files --- so say in a chunk I create a vector 
txt = sample(list.files(directory,full.names=T),n,replace=F) 
then I'd like to be able to do something like

## This is part of the main .Rnw file
...
\begin{itemize}
\item 
<<child=\Sexpr{txt[1]>>=
@

\item 
<<child=\Sexpr{txt[2]>>=
@
...
\end{document}
# End of the main .Rnw file.

This construction doesn't work --- but is there a clever way to do something like this?

Thanks!
Gianluca

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] child variable filename?
parts:
It is very straightforward -- just child=txt[1]. There is no need to
use \Sexpr{}. Chunk options are treated as pure R code, and any valid
R code works there.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
